text.cover: The Snug. A story about belonging and making room for everyone.
text.p01: To everyone still waiting at the edge of the meadow: you can build a place of your own.
text.p04: In Bramble Hollow, when the first cold wind blew, all the animals squeezed together under the Big Oak, warm and giggling.
text.p05: Bodie the badger loved it best of all. He pulled on his blue hat, wiggled in close, and sighed, "Snug!"
text.p06: One misty evening, a little cart creaked down the lane. A new family was moving into the empty burrow by the hill.
text.p07: Out stepped Quilla, a young porcupine in a yellow neckerchief. When she felt shy, her quills stood straight up.
text.p08: The next day, Quilla walked to the Big Oak. "Hello," she said softly. "May I squeeze in too?"
text.p09: But everyone scooted away. "Too prickly!" whispered the rabbit twins. So Quilla sat all alone at the edge of the meadow.
text.p10: Bodie saw her sitting there. He wanted to go over, but his tummy did a flip-flop. What if they scooted away from him, too?
text.p11: He took a deep breath, walked all the way across the meadow, and sat right down beside her. "Hello," said Bodie.
text.p12: They sat for a long time, watching the others under the oak. Then Quilla said, "I'm done waiting to be asked."
text.p13: "Let's make a warm place of our own. Right here." Bodie grinned. "I can dig!" "And I can climb!" said Quilla.
text.p14: Bodie scooped a round, deep hollow. Quilla climbed high and tugged down long, bendy vines. "Scoop, loop, snug!" they sang.
text.p15: They looped the vines into walls. A loose quill fell out, like a baby tooth. "A pin!" said Quilla, and pinned them tight.
text.p16: Hazel the squirrel hopped by. "What are you making?" "A snug!" said Bodie. "Ooh! Can I help?" asked Hazel.
text.p17: Hazel piled soft moss on the roof. Thimble the mouse tied every vine with tiny, tidy knots. Scoop, loop, snug!
text.p18: Mossy the mole popped up right in the middle of the floor. "Did somebody say dig?" He smoothed it flat and cozy.
text.p19: Scoop, loop, snug! Five friends, one snug. When the cold wind came whooshing, the walls didn't wobble one bit.
text.p20: At last it was done. They hung acorn-cup lanterns by the door. "It's beautiful," whispered Quilla. "Who is it for?" asked Hazel.
text.p21: Quilla thought about the Big Oak, and all the scooting away. Then she smiled her biggest smile. "Everyone," she said. "It's for everyone."
text.p22: That evening, the first snowflakes fell. Bodie called across the meadow, "The Snug is open! Everyone is welcome!" And everyone came.
text.p23: The rabbit twins stopped at the door, ears drooping. "We're sorry we scooted," said Fern. "Is there room for us?"
text.p24: Quilla held the door open wide. "Lots of room," she said. "Come in, come in!" And they all squeezed in together.
text.p25: Outside, the snow fell softly. Inside, Bodie sighed, "Snug." If there's no room for you, build a place with room for everyone. The End.
